channels.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect {name}? Existing chat history is preserved, but the bot will stop forwarding new messages to this agent.
channels.telegramDescription: Talk to @BotFather on Telegram, run /newbot, and paste the HTTP API token it returns. The token is verified via getMe before anything is saved.
channels.telegramConnectedInfo: Bot is live as <link>@{username}</link>. Send it a message on Telegram to test the integration.
channels.discordDescription: Open the Discord Developer Portal, create an application, add a Bot, and copy the Bot Token. Make sure MESSAGE CONTENT INTENT is enabled under Bot → Privileged Gateway Intents. The token is verified via /users/@me before anything is saved.
channels.discordConnectedInfo: Bot is live as <mono>{username}</mono>. Invite it to a server (OAuth2 → URL Generator → Bot scope) or DM it on Discord to test.
channels.slackDescription: Create a Slack app at api.slack.com/apps. Enable Socket Mode, generate an app-level token (xapp-…) with connections:write, then under OAuth & Permissions copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…). Then go to Event Subscriptions → Subscribe to bot events and add message.channels, message.im, and app_mention (Slack will prompt for the matching scopes — channels:history, im:history, app_mentions:read — and ask you to reinstall).
channels.slackConnectedInfo: Bot is live in workspace {team}. Invite it to a channel with /invite @bot and message it to test.
channels.lineDescription: Create a Messaging API channel at developers.line.biz. Under Messaging API issue a long-lived Channel access token, and copy the Channel secret from the Basic settings tab. Toggle on Use webhook after saving the URL we'll generate.
channels.lineWebhookInstructions: Paste this into LINE Developers Console → Messaging API → Webhook URL, click Verify, then toggle Use webhook on.
channels.lineTestHint: Add the bot as a friend (search the basic ID), or invite it to a group, then send a message to test.
channels.lineSecretHint: Optional but strongly recommended — fastclaw verifies inbound webhook payloads via HMAC-SHA256 against this secret.
channels.wechatDescription: Scan the QR code with the WeChat phone app to bind a personal WeChat account as the bot for this agent. Inbound DMs will be relayed to the agent; the agent's replies are sent back as plain text.
channels.wechatConnectedInfo: Bot is live as {id}. Send it a WeChat message to test.
channels.feishuDescription: Create a custom app at open.feishu.cn. Enable the bot capability, request im:message + im:message:send_as_bot scopes, then copy the App ID + App Secret from Credentials & Basic Info. Long-connection mode (recommended) needs nothing else; webhook mode also needs the Verification Token / Encrypt Key from Event Subscriptions.
channels.feishuLongConnHint: fastclaw opens a WebSocket to Feishu — no public URL required. Turn off to use the classic webhook flow.
channels.feishuLongConnConnectedInfo: fastclaw is now opening a WebSocket to Feishu — no public URL setup needed. In the Feishu Developer Console under 事件与回调 → 事件配置 → 订阅方式, pick 使用长连接接收事件, then under Subscribe to bot events add im.message.receive_v1.
channels.feishuWebhookInstructions: Paste this into Feishu Developer Console → Event Subscriptions → Request URL, then click Save. Feishu will POST a verification challenge here and this fastclaw instance will echo it automatically.
channels.feishuVerificationTokenHint: Optional but recommended — fastclaw rejects webhook payloads whose header.token doesn't match.
channels.feishuEncryptKeyPlaceholder: leave empty if 加密策略 is not configured
channels.feishuEncryptKeyHint: Only required if you set an Encrypt Key under 加密策略 in the Feishu console. Empty = expect plaintext webhook bodies.

context.title: Context
context.subtitle: What the LLM sees for {name}. The prompt mode picks both the framework prompt profile and the built-in tool set. Custom tools come from plugins — always exposed regardless of mode.
context.modeAgentDesc: Agent — full framework prompt (task delegation, tool-use discipline, workspace self-update, scheduling) + all built-in tools. Default for autonomous task agents.
context.modeChatbotDesc: Chatbot — slim framework so persona files shape voice directly. Built-ins narrowed to image_gen, tts, write_file, edit_file — the last two let the LLM persist USER.md / MEMORY.md when it learns about the chatter. Memory is the USER.md / MEMORY.md sections inlined in the system prompt; no memory_search escape hatch (it scans logs chatbot mode doesn't write, returns empty, and confuses the model). Main reply emits as plain text, multi-bubble via the inline split marker. For companion / role-play / customer-support bots.
context.modeCustomizeDesc: Customize — only the date anchor + your bootstrap files; NO built-in tools. You write the system prompt completely via SOUL.md / IDENTITY.md and bring tools via plugins.
context.pluginNote: Plugin and MCP tools are always exposed regardless of mode. Build a plugin — see ~/.fastclaw/plugins/fastclaw-plugin-demo for a minimal example.
context.multiBubbleDesc: Let the agent split one reply into multiple chat bubbles using a separator marker — natural for short, multi-beat replies in IM. Applies to every IM channel (WeChat / Telegram / Discord / Slack / LINE / Feishu); ignored on web. Off by default — keeps each reply as a single message.
context.autoRememberDesc: Backup persistence path: every 5 user-turns the runtime fires a small LLM call that distills the recent conversation into USER.md / MEMORY.md. The primary path is the LLM writing those files directly via write_file / edit_file (now available in Chatbot mode too) — this toggle just makes sure something still gets persisted when the model forgets to. Off by default to preserve the stateless-across-sessions behavior.
context.sharedIdentityDesc: When enabled, all IM channels (WeChat / Telegram / Discord / Slack / LINE / Feishu) share the same session and memory with the web chat. Conversations started on one channel can be continued on another. Off by default — each channel gets its own isolated session and memory.
